recipes.name: Zucchini Cornbread Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (8.5 ounce) package dry corn muffin mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart baking dish with cooking spray.

Mix together zucchini, onion, muffin mix, beaten eggs, salt, and pepper in a large bowl until well combined. Stir in 4 ounces cheese. Spread evenly into the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle with remaining 4 ounces cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is lightly browned and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Cornbread Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This cornbread zucchini casserole features shredded squash baked with onion, corn muffin mix, and Cheddar cheese for a yummy, comforting side dish.

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe two times. The first - per the instructions. It was way to wet, but good flavor. The second time I grated the zucchini and lightly salted it and put it in a collander for about an hour. I squeezed the zucchini at the end of that time before adding it to the recipe. (I had over a cup of liquid!) I also added all the cheese to the mix instead of using half for the top. Now it was great!!

Great recipe and good use of zucchini! Light, fluffy, excellent cornbread! Company loved it!!! Update: You must drain the zucchini... lightly salt the zucchini and let sit for 15 min minimally to weep the zucchini. Press out any remaining water before adding it to your mix. Additions you can add to enhance the flavor: grilled corn off the cob, diced sweet red pepper, green ortega chili's, onion, or any type of spicy cheese.

Delicious! I squeezed about 1 cup of liquid from the shredded zucchini, added 6 tbsp melted butter, and only needed to bake for 35 minutes (def not 60). It’s now my new favorite. Next time, I want to add corn kernels. Thank you!! 🤌🧡🙏

This was excellent. I added some chopped jalapeños. Sautéed the onions & jalapeños before adding to zucchini. Definitely salted, drained & pressed water from zucchini in a colander. I doubled recipe & used 9x13 casserole dish. This was a perfect complement to enchiladas or taco meal.

My fiance and I both really liked this tasty and unique casserole. I used a sweet onion, Jiffy mix, a 7 oz bag of extra sharp Sargento cheddar, and 6 zucchini, which equaled 4 shredded cups almost exactly. I didn't have an issue with the muffin mix being sweet; I thought it worked well with the sharpness of the onion, the cracked pepper, and the savory cheese. Note purely for myself: cooked at 65 minutes @ 355. Would cook at a slightly higher temperature for slightly longer, in order to further bake the cheese.

Absolutely follow the advice of the first review that pops up - salt and rest the zucchini for a while, then squeeze the moisture out of it. Because I did this, I did not add salt to the recipe. I also added the cheese to the entire dish rather than topping it with cheese. It was savory and delicious, I will definitely make it again.

This recipe is AMAZING!! It's probably my favorite that I've tried from AllRecipes thus far. My husband and I gobbled up every bit of it and my 10 month old daughter loved it as well! I agree that the zucchini should be drained as it helped to keep the moisture down. I added 2 tsp of minced garlic to our version and sautéed the onions with some sweet peppers before adding them to the mix. I baked it in a 9x9" pan and accidentally over baked it, which gave it a nice crusty top. Delicious!

This was really good! I did as some others had done and after shredding the zucchini I added about 1/4t salt and let it sit over a colander for about an hour, stirring it every 15 mins or so. I got a good 1/4 of water off of it. Didn't add anymore salt to the recipe and added all of the cheese inside rather than some on top. It was done in about 45 mins - probably less than the 60 stated because I had gotten rid of the zucchini moisture. It came out great - would definitely make again.

Sooo good!! Made this to go with BBQ baby back ribs and it was a hit. We love spicy so I added grilled corn off the cob, a Serrano Chile with all seeds for good heat, green bell peppers, red onion, green onion and minced garlic clove. I added all 8oz of sharp cheddar in casserole and topped casserole with 4oz of Colby jack. AMAZING!! I did take recommendation from others and lightly salted zucchini to help remove water. This worked great! My hubby thinks this would be great casserole for thanksgiving side!!

Very easy to make. Used a spicey cheddar and a 15oz box of krusteaz corn bread mix. Also added added a 1/3 cup of milk. Salt the zucchini and let sit in a colander for at least 30 min , then rinse and squeeze out excess water (someone posted this suggestion and it worked well).

This was delicious!! I added some roasted red pepper and roasted corn (I had some leftover from the previous night's dinner). Not only did it add good flavor, it made the dish colorful. I, too, salted and drained the zucchini before adding it in. It cooked the full hour, so the liquid could be absorbed and THEN I added extra cheese on top (which I didn't feel was necessary). I will make this again.
Texture was ok.
Brown ground hamburger/pork/turkey for a little carnivore kick.

This was delicious! I halved the recipe and did salt and drain the zucchini and added some diced red pepper and sauteed with the onion. I also added a tsp each of garlic powder and chives. Baked for almost 50 minutes. I will definitely make this dish again!
I loved it
I added 1 pound of cooked breakfast sausage for a delicious breakfast casserole.
Very good, as always. If you have a garden this is a recipe you'll make more than once. I did salt and drain and squeeze.

I made this nearly as written, I subbed a gluten free cornbread mix to make the recipe gluten free. I was not sure how much onion to use so I used half of a large yellow onion. Baking for 60 minutes was perfect timing (I used a 9x13 glass pan). Unfortunately for different reasons this recipe was not a hit in my house. The amount of onions was one of the big complaints along with the squashy taste. I am a huge fan of zucchini but I wasn't a fan of this recipe, something just wasn't right. My family rated this everywhere from 1-3 so I split my rating in the middle.

This dish is the bomb! It's a good thing the kids are gone because hubby and I blew through this dish in no time. The only thing I did different was to sauteed my onions in butter before adding them to the mix. I'm making it again tonight but adding diced, cooked chicken. I also have some left over beef roast that I'll try next time. There's just something about cornbread!

I made this from another recipe calling for 16 oz of cheese. We decided (before seeing this post) that although ours was good, it would be much better with 8 oz of cheese. Allowing zucchini juice to drain may also increase the texture in a positive way
